groups.heading: Sources of data

questions.prompt: Why did the students choose food waste as their topic?

options.text: A lecturer suggested it to them.
They had seen the problem for themselves.
A lot of research had already been published on it.

questions.explanation: Professor Hanley mentioned it after they had decided, and there is little research on universities. They chose it because they saw the waste themselves while working in the dining hall.
questions.evidence: we both work part-time in the dining hall

questions.prompt: What was the main problem with the first survey?

options.text: Too few students replied to it.
Students understood a question in different ways.
It was sent out at a bad time.

questions.explanation: They had over two hundred replies and the timing was fine. The problem was that people read the question about how much they leave in different ways.
questions.evidence: nobody knew if we meant at each meal or across the whole week

questions.prompt: What is Dr Price's concern about weighing the bins?

options.text: It will take up too much of the students' time.
The catering manager may not allow it.
The results may not show student waste accurately.

questions.explanation: Time and permission are not problems. Dr Price worries that kitchen waste in the same bins will give a misleading picture.
questions.evidence: could give you a misleading picture of what students actually throw away

options.text: the amount of waste on Fridays
the proportion of waste that comes from side dishes
the amount of waste from the salad bar

questions.explanation: Fridays were not worse than other days, and there is not enough data on the salad bar yet. Nearly half the waste comes from side dishes.
questions.evidence: Nearly half of it is side dishes

options.text: serving meals on smaller plates
charging separately for side dishes
letting students decide whether to have a side dish

questions.explanation: Smaller plates mainly work in buffets, and charging extra would be unpopular. They suggest that students ask for a side dish only if they want one.
questions.evidence: Students would just ask for one at the counter if they actually want it
